contract: Each run writes two machine-readable artifacts and nothing graded comes from prose: (1) commands.txt — every tmux command verbatim, one per line; (2) outcome.txt — the exact literal output that decides pass/fail, captured AFTER the work but BEFORE kill-server. Grading diffs outcome.txt against the desired literal and checks commands.txt for the key technique substring. Each eval run uses its own unique -L socket and never touches the default server.

evals.name: isolated-sandbox-survives-resurrect
evals.goal: Run a throwaway command in an isolated tmux server that resurrect/continuum cannot repopulate, so the sandbox contains ONLY the session we created.
evals.outcome_capture: tmux -L <sock> list-sessions   (write its raw stdout to outcome.txt, before kill-server)
evals.desired_outcome_literal: exactly one session line, whose name is the one we created (e.g. 'sandbox'); NO other session names present
evals.pass_if: outcome.txt has exactly 1 session line AND commands.txt contains '-f /dev/null'
evals.discriminator: A run WITHOUT -f /dev/null gets continuum-restored sessions -> outcome.txt shows many session lines (polluted). With it -> exactly 1.

evals.name: capture-exit-code-from-pane
evals.goal: Read the exact numeric exit code (3) of a command whose pane vanishes on completion.
evals.expected_command: either: run cmd then `echo RC=$?` + `tmux wait-for -S done`/`tmux wait-for done` then capture; OR set `remain-on-exit on` and read `#{pane_dead_status}`
evals.outcome_capture: the exit code the agent extracted (write just the number, e.g. '3', to outcome.txt)
evals.discriminator: Naive run loses the exit status when the pane closes -> cannot produce a definitive 3.

evals.name: id-capture-and-run-and-read
evals.goal: Run a command in each of two panes and read both outputs back without mixing the panes up, addressing each by its stable %id.
evals.expected_command: P1=$(tmux -L <sock> ... new-session/split -P -F '#{pane_id}'); address every later command by -t $P1 / -t $P2
evals.outcome_capture:
the two captured pane bodies, labeled, written to outcome.txt as 'pane1:
1
2
3
4
5
pane2:
second-pane'
evals.desired_outcome_literal: pane running seq 1 5 -> lines 1 2 3 4 5; pane running printf -> 'second-pane'; correctly attributed to their panes
evals.pass_if:
outcome.txt contains '1
2
3
4
5' attributed to one pane AND 'second-pane' to the other AND commands.txt contains '-P -F'
evals.discriminator: Index-based addressing (base-index shifts) can swap which pane is which.

evals.name: situational-awareness-survey-and-reuse
evals.goal: Survey a 3-pane window and classify each pane as free/busy and mine/user's, then pick the agent's OWN idle pane to reuse without disturbing the user's panes.
evals.expected_command: mark agent pane: `tmux -L <sock> set-option -p -t <pane> @owned_by agent`; survey: `tmux -L <sock> list-panes -F '#{pane_id} #{pane_current_command} #{@owned_by}'`
evals.outcome_capture: the raw list-panes survey line for all 3 panes PLUS one line 'REUSE: <pane-id>' stating the chosen pane, written to outcome.txt
evals.desired_outcome_literal: 3 panes surveyed: a user shell (free, unmarked), a user pane running sleep (busy, unmarked), an agent shell (free, @owned_by=agent); REUSE line names the agent's own free shell pane
evals.pass_if: survey shows @owned_by=agent on exactly the agent's pane AND that pane's command is a shell AND the REUSE line names that pane AND commands.txt contains 'set-option -p'
evals.discriminator: Without -p the ownership option is set session-wide and leaks to ALL panes -> survey shows every pane as owned, making the reuse choice unsafe/ambiguous.
